question:
The following sentence has been divided into three segments. One of them may contain an adverbial usage error. Select the option that has the segment with the error. If you don't find any error, select 'No error' as your answer.
Mrs. Arunima / speaks / Telugu well.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Mrs. Arunima speaks Telugu well" is a simple, grammatically correct sentence in the Simple Present Tense.

• Rule — Position of Adverbs of Manner: An adverb of manner (like "well") that modifies a verb is correctly placed after the verb and its object, i.e., Subject + Verb + Object + Adverb.

• Applying the rule: "speaks" (verb) + "Telugu" (object) + "well" (adverb of manner) — this is the standard and correct word order in English.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "speaks" is incorrect because this segment is not the source of any error — the verb correctly agrees with the singular subject "Mrs. Arunima" (third person singular, so "speaks" and not "speak").

• Option 2: "Mrs. Arunima" is incorrect because the subject is correctly stated with no grammatical fault.

• Option 3: "Telugu well." is incorrect because the object "Telugu" followed by the adverb "well" is in the correct order; there is no misplacement here.

NOTE

• Adverbs of manner (well, badly, slowly, carefully) usually come after the verb/object, not between the verb and the object (e.g., "He speaks English well" NOT "He speaks well English").

• Common SSC trap: confusing adverb placement errors with subject-verb agreement errors — always check both possibilities before marking 'No error'.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
According to the encyclopaedia, a oasis is an area which is made fertile by a source of freshwater.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. a oasis is an area.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rule — Use of "a" and "an": The article "an" is used before a word that begins with a vowel sound, while "a" is used before a word that begins with a consonant sound.

• The word "oasis" begins with the vowel sound /oʊ/, so it must be preceded by "an", not "a".

• Applying the rule: "a oasis" is incorrect and must be corrected to "an oasis".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "a source of freshwater." is incorrect because this segment contains no grammatical error; "a source" is correct since "source" begins with a consonant sound.

• Option 3: "According to the encyclopaedia," is incorrect because this introductory phrase is correctly formed and punctuated.

• Option 4: "which is made fertile by" is incorrect because this relative clause is correctly formed with the correct passive structure.

NOTE

• The choice of "a" or "an" depends on sound, not spelling — e.g., "an hour" (silent h) but "a university" (consonant sound /j/).

• Other commonly confused words: "an heir", "an honest man", "a European", "a one-rupee note".

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
He have / workers from / Ireland and France / in his factory.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. He have.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement: A singular subject in the third person (like "He") must be followed by the singular form of the verb "has", not the plural form "have", in the Simple Present Tense.

• Applying the rule: "He have" is grammatically incorrect and must be corrected to "He has".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "in his factory." is incorrect because this prepositional phrase is correctly formed.

• Option 2: "workers from" is incorrect because this segment is grammatically sound.

• Option 3: "Ireland and France" is incorrect because the proper nouns are correctly stated with no error.

NOTE

• Singular subjects (he, she, it, and singular nouns) take "has" in the Simple Present Tense; plural subjects and "I/you/we/they" take "have".

• This is one of the most frequently tested subject-verb agreement errors in SSC exams.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Sarita speaks French best.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. well.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Sarita speaks French best." wrongly uses the superlative degree "best" even though no comparison among three or more people is being made.

• Rule — Degrees of Comparison: The superlative degree is used only when comparing three or more persons/things. When no such comparison is stated, the positive degree of the adverb must be used.

• Applying the rule: since the sentence is not comparing Sarita's French-speaking ability with two or more other people, the superlative "best" must be replaced with the positive degree adverb "well".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "worst" is incorrect because this is the superlative degree of a negative adverb, which does not fit the context and is grammatically just as wrong as "best" here.

• Option 2: "better" is incorrect because "better" is the comparative degree, used to compare exactly two persons/things, but no such comparison is indicated in the sentence.

• Option 3: "good" is incorrect because "good" is an adjective, not an adverb, and cannot modify the verb "speaks"; the adverb form "well" is required.

NOTE

• Positive degree: well; Comparative degree: better (than one other); Superlative degree: best (among three or more).

• Common SSC trap: sentences that describe a general/habitual ability (with no explicit comparison) should use the positive degree, not the superlative.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Family plays a vital role in our lives, serving as a source of love, support, and stability. It is (1)________ the family unit that we develop lasting bonds, learn essential values, and find comfort during (2) ________ times. Families provide a nurturing environment for personal growth and emotional well-being. They (3) ________ guidance, share experiences, and create cherished memories. The strength and (4) ________ of a family contribute to individual happiness, societal harmony, and the (5) ________ of a strong community.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. within.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence uses the cleft structure "It is ... that ...", which is used to emphasise a particular part of a sentence.

• The context requires a preposition indicating that the bonding, values, and comfort are developed inside/as part of the family unit itself, not outside it.

• The preposition "within" correctly conveys the sense of "inside" or "as an internal part of" the family unit, which fits the meaning of the passage.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "among" is incorrect because "among" is used for a distributive relationship involving more than two members of a group, and does not fit the sense of "inside" the family unit as a whole.

• Option 3: "beyond" is incorrect because it means "outside the limits of," which contradicts the passage's meaning that these bonds are developed inside the family unit.

• Option 4: "between" is incorrect because "between" is generally used for two people/things, and does not fit the intended meaning of "inside the family unit."

NOTE

• "Within" = inside the limits of (time, space, or a group); "Beyond" = outside the limits of; "Between" = involving two; "Among" = involving more than two, distributed.

• In cloze passages, always read the full sentence and surrounding context to choose the preposition that fits the intended meaning, not just grammatical correctness.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Family plays a vital role in our lives, serving as a source of love, support, and stability. It is (1)________ the family unit that we develop lasting bonds, learn essential values, and find comfort during (2) ________ times. Families provide a nurturing environment for personal growth and emotional well-being. They (3) ________ guidance, share experiences, and create cherished memories. The strength and (4) ________ of a family contribute to individual happiness, societal harmony, and the (5) ________ of a strong community.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. challenging.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence states that families provide **"comfort during ________ times,"** implying that comfort is needed at a time when things are difficult.

• The word "challenging" means difficult or demanding, which logically fits the idea that people seek comfort from family during hard times.

• The overall tone of the passage is positive and supportive, describing the family as a source of comfort in difficult situations.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "joyful" is incorrect because comfort is typically sought during difficult times, not joyful ones; the context does not fit.

• Option 3: "initial" is incorrect because "initial" means "first" or "beginning," which does not logically describe a time when comfort is required.

• Option 4: "wasteful" is incorrect because "wasteful" describes an unnecessary or extravagant use of something, and cannot describe a period of time in this context.

NOTE

• Cloze questions often test contextual meaning rather than grammar alone — always check which word logically completes the idea of the sentence.

• Common word pairs tested in SSC cloze passages: challenging/difficult, comfort/support, hardship/adversity.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Family plays a vital role in our lives, serving as a source of love, support, and stability. It is (1)________ the family unit that we develop lasting bonds, learn essential values, and find comfort during (2) ________ times. Families provide a nurturing environment for personal growth and emotional well-being. They (3) ________ guidance, share experiences, and create cherished memories. The strength and (4) ________ of a family contribute to individual happiness, societal harmony, and the (5) ________ of a strong community.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. offer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: **"They ________ guidance, share experiences, and create cherished memories,"** describing positive actions that families perform for their members.

• The verb "offer" collocates naturally with the noun "guidance" — "offer guidance" is a standard, idiomatic collocation in English meaning to provide advice or direction.

• The verb must also be parallel in meaning with the other listed actions — "share experiences" and "create memories" — all of which are giving/nurturing actions, matching "offer guidance."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "deliver" is incorrect because "deliver guidance" is not a natural or standard English collocation; "deliver" collocates with things like "deliver a speech" or "deliver a verdict."

• Option 3: "contribute" is incorrect because "contribute" requires a preposition like "to" (e.g., "contribute to guidance"), and cannot directly take "guidance" as its object in this sense.

• Option 4: "propose" is incorrect because "propose guidance" is not idiomatic; "propose" collocates with ideas, plans, or marriage proposals, not with "guidance."

NOTE

• Collocation-based cloze questions test which verb "naturally pairs" with a noun in standard English usage — common ones include: offer guidance, give advice, provide support, share experiences.

• Learning common verb-noun collocations is essential for scoring well in SSC cloze/fill-in-the-blank questions.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Family plays a vital role in our lives, serving as a source of love, support, and stability. It is (1)________ the family unit that we develop lasting bonds, learn essential values, and find comfort during (2) ________ times. Families provide a nurturing environment for personal growth and emotional well-being. They (3) ________ guidance, share experiences, and create cherished memories. The strength and (4) ________ of a family contribute to individual happiness, societal harmony, and the (5) ________ of a strong community.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. cohesion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: **"The strength and ________ of a family contribute to individual happiness, societal harmony...,"** which requires a positive quality that, paired with "strength," describes a well-bonded family.

• The word "cohesion" means the state of sticking together as one unit; unity, which pairs naturally with "strength" to describe a family that stays firmly bonded together.

• The word must fit the positive tone of the passage, which describes the benefits of a strong, united family.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "intrusion" is incorrect because it means "an unwelcome interruption," a negative quality that contradicts the positive tone of the sentence.

• Option 3: "disruption" is incorrect because it means "disturbance or interruption," which is the opposite of unity and does not fit the sentence's positive context.

• Option 4: "commotion" is incorrect because it means "noisy confusion or disturbance," which does not describe a positive family quality contributing to societal harmony.

NOTE

• "Cohesion" (unity, sticking together) is often contrasted with "disruption/discord" (division, disturbance) in SSC vocabulary-based cloze questions.

• Related word: "cohesive" (adjective) — e.g., "a cohesive team works well together."

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Family plays a vital role in our lives, serving as a source of love, support, and stability. It is (1)________ the family unit that we develop lasting bonds, learn essential values, and find comfort during (2) ________ times. Families provide a nurturing environment for personal growth and emotional well-being. They (3) ________ guidance, share experiences, and create cherished memories. The strength and (4) ________ of a family contribute to individual happiness, societal harmony, and the (5) ________ of a strong community.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. foundation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence concludes the passage: **"...contribute to individual happiness, societal harmony, and the ________ of a strong community,"** requiring a word that shows family as the base on which a community is built.

• The word "foundation" means the basis or groundwork on which something is built, which fits perfectly with the idea that families are the building blocks of a strong community.

• This maintains the positive, constructive tone established throughout the passage about the role of family.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "undermining" is incorrect because it means "weakening or damaging gradually," a negative meaning that contradicts the passage's positive tone.

• Option 3: "collision" is incorrect because it means "a violent clash or conflict," which does not logically fit the idea of building a strong community.

• Option 4: "erosion" is incorrect because it means "gradual wearing away or destruction," which is the opposite of building a strong community.

NOTE

• "Foundation" (basis, groundwork) is often contrasted with negative words like "erosion," "undermining," and "collapse" in SSC vocabulary tests.

• Related idiom: "to lay the foundation of something" = to establish the basic groundwork for something.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Forbidden
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Allowed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Forbidden" means not permitted or not allowed; prohibited. (निषिद्ध)
◦ Example: Smoking is forbidden inside the hospital premises.

• Its most appropriate antonym among the given options is "Allowed", which means permitted or given permission to do something. (अनुमति प्राप्त)
◦ Example: Visitors are allowed inside the museum only with a valid ticket.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Protected" (सुरक्षित): Kept safe from harm; this is not opposite in meaning to "forbidden."

• Option 2: "Prevented" (रोका गया): Stopped from happening; this is close in meaning to "forbidden," not its opposite.

• Option 3: "Banned" (प्रतिबंधित): This is actually a synonym of "forbidden," not its antonym.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Forbidden": prohibited, banned, proscribed, outlawed.

• Other antonyms of "Forbidden": permitted, sanctioned, authorised.

question:
Identify the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word based on the context of the sentence.
He gave a haughty consent without honouring him with a single word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Modest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "haughty" means arrogantly proud; showing excessive pride and contempt for others. (घमंडी)
◦ Example: She gave a haughty look to the waiter who had made a small mistake.

• Its most appropriate contextual antonym is "Modest", which means humble in behaviour, not proud or arrogant. (विनम्र)
◦ Example: Despite winning the award, he remained modest about his achievement.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Proud" (घमंडी): This is a near-synonym of "haughty," not its antonym.

• Option 2: "Happy" (खुश): This describes an emotional state and is unrelated to the sense of pride/arrogance conveyed by "haughty."

• Option 4: "Indifferent" (उदासीन): This means "showing no interest or concern," which is not the opposite of "haughty" (arrogant pride).

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "haughty": arrogant, supercilious, disdainful, snobbish.

• Other antonyms of "haughty": humble, meek, unassuming, unpretentious.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
We have carried out an successful raid on a fraudulent minister.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. a successful raid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rule — Use of "a" and "an": The article "a" is used before a word beginning with a consonant sound, while "an" is used before a word beginning with a vowel sound.

• The word "successful" begins with the consonant sound /s/ (pronounced "suh"), so it must be preceded by "a", not "an".

• Applying the rule: "an successful raid" is incorrect and must be corrected to "a successful raid".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "the successful raid" is incorrect because "the" is used for a specific, previously mentioned or unique noun, but here the raid is being mentioned for the first time, so the indefinite article "a" is required.

• Option 2: "successful raid" is incorrect because a singular countable noun ("raid") must always be preceded by an article ("a" or "the"); omitting the article altogether is ungrammatical here.

• Option 3: "these successful raid" is incorrect because "these" is a plural demonstrative pronoun and cannot be used with the singular noun "raid" (it would require "these successful raids").

NOTE

• The choice between "a" and "an" depends on the sound, not the spelling, of the following word — e.g., "a university" (consonant sound /j/), "an hour" (silent h).

• Demonstrative pronouns "this/these" and "that/those" must always agree in number with the noun they modify.

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given sentence.
They were good-hearted girls, unclean, clothed in rags and profiundly ignorant.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Profiundly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Profoundly" — meaning very greatly or intensely; deeply.
◦ Example: The speech left the audience profoundly moved.

• Spelling key: PRO + FOUND + LY. The word is formed from "profound" (deep, intense) + the adverb suffix "-ly." The given word "Profiundly" wrongly places an "i" in place of the "o" of "found."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Hearted" is correctly spelt and forms part of the correctly spelt compound adjective "good-hearted."

• Option 3: "Unclean" is correctly spelt, meaning "not clean" or "dirty."

• Option 4: "Clothed" is correctly spelt, meaning "dressed" or "covered with clothes."

NOTE

• The related adjective is "profound" and the related noun is "profundity."

• Other commonly misspelt "-ly" adverbs in SSC exams: definitely, separately, immediately, occasionally.

question:
Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank.
The hospital is ________ the river.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. by.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence requires a preposition indicating location or proximity — "The hospital is ________ the river" means the hospital is located near/beside the river.

• The word "by" is a preposition meaning "near" or "beside," which correctly completes the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "buy" is incorrect because it is a verb meaning "to purchase something," which does not fit grammatically or contextually here.

• Option 3: "bye" is incorrect because it is used as a short form of "goodbye" and does not function as a preposition of location.

• Option 4: "bi" is incorrect because it is a prefix meaning "two" (as in "bicycle" or "bimonthly") and cannot function as a standalone word in this sentence.

NOTE

• "Buy," "by," and "bye" are classic homophones (words that sound alike but have different meanings and spellings) frequently tested in SSC exams.

• Other common homophone sets: their/there/they're, to/too/two, write/right, know/no.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Erudite
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Educated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Erudite" means having or showing great knowledge or learning; scholarly. (विद्वान)
◦ Example: The professor gave an erudite lecture on ancient Indian history.

• Its closest synonym among the given options is "Educated", which means having received formal schooling or training; knowledgeable. (शिक्षित)
◦ Example: She comes from a highly educated family of doctors and lawyers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Humble" (विनम्र): Means "modest, not proud," which is unrelated to the sense of learning conveyed by "erudite."

• Option 2: "Honest" (ईमानदार): Means "truthful, sincere," which does not relate to scholarly knowledge.

• Option 3: "Strong" (मजबूत): Means "physically or mentally powerful," which is unrelated to the meaning of "erudite."

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Erudite": learned, scholarly, well-read, knowledgeable, cultured.

• Antonym of "Erudite": ignorant, uneducated, illiterate.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Fish out of water
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To be out of place.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Fish out of water" means to feel awkward or uncomfortable in an unfamiliar situation or environment; to be out of place. (अनजान माहौल में असहज महसूस करना)
◦ Example: At the formal dinner party, the young boy felt like a fish out of water.

• The expression draws its imagery from the fact that a fish, which naturally belongs in water, would be completely helpless and disoriented if taken out of it — just as a person feels in an unfamiliar setting.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "No knowledge of marine life" is a literal misinterpretation of the idiom and is not its actual figurative meaning.

• Option 3: "To die soon" is incorrect; this is not the meaning conveyed by this idiom, though a fish literally taken out of water might die — the idiom is used figuratively for discomfort, not death.

• Option 4: "Not good at swimming" is incorrect; this is a literal misreading of the idiom and does not reflect its figurative meaning.

NOTE

• Other common idioms with animal imagery tested in SSC exams: "A fish out of water" (out of place), "To smell a rat" (to suspect something wrong), "To let the cat out of the bag" (to reveal a secret), "To kill two birds with one stone" (to achieve two things at once).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Comendation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Commendation" — meaning an act of formally praising someone; an award or official recognition of merit.
◦ Example: The soldier received a commendation for his bravery.

• Spelling key: COM + MEND + ATION — note the double "m" (com + mend). The given word "Comendation" incorrectly drops one "m."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Reimbursement" is correctly spelt, meaning "repayment of money spent or lost."

• Option 3: "Competition" is correctly spelt, meaning "a contest between rivals."

• Option 4: "Intertwined" is correctly spelt, meaning "twisted together; closely connected."

NOTE

• The related verb is "commend" (to praise formally) and the related adjective is "commendable" (praiseworthy).

• Other words commonly misspelt by dropping a double letter in SSC exams: "accommodation," "recommend," "occurrence," "embarrassment."

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The ________ today will be cloudy and humid.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. weather.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence describes atmospheric conditions — "cloudy and humid" — which are terms used to describe the weather.

• The word "weather" means the state of the atmosphere at a particular place and time, in terms of temperature, cloud, rain, etc., which correctly completes the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "wither" is incorrect because it is a verb meaning "to become dry and shrivelled" (usually of a plant), which does not fit the context.

• Option 2: "waiter" is incorrect because it means "a person who serves food in a restaurant," which is unrelated to the context of the sentence.

• Option 4: "whether" is incorrect because it is a conjunction used to express doubt or choice between alternatives (e.g., "I don't know whether it will rain"), and cannot function as the subject of the sentence here.

NOTE

• "Weather" and "whether" are commonly confused homophones (similar pronunciation) frequently tested in SSC exams — "weather" relates to climate, "whether" introduces a choice/doubt.

• Other similar-sounding word pairs: "wither/whither," "waiver/waver."

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Yoga may manage pain and helping reduce stress.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. help in reducing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence has the structure "Yoga may manage pain and [X] stress," where the modal "may" governs both actions joined by "and."

• Rule — Parallelism with Modal Verbs: When a modal verb (may/can/will, etc.) governs two or more verbs joined by "and," both verbs must be grammatically compatible with the modal and correctly structured for the sentence to make sense.

• Applying the rule: "Yoga may manage pain and [may] help in reducing stress" — here "help" correctly follows the modal "may," and "in reducing" (preposition + gerund) is the correct grammatical structure to follow "help" when expressing purpose/contribution.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "help reduction for" is incorrect because "reduction for stress" is not idiomatic; the correct preposition would be "reduction of stress," and this phrasing is awkward and non-standard.

• Option 2: "helped reduce" is incorrect because the past tense "helped" breaks the parallel structure with the modal "may," which requires a base verb form.

• Option 3: "help reduced" is incorrect because "reduced" (past tense/past participle) cannot directly follow "help" in this construction; it is grammatically unsound.

NOTE

• "Help" can be followed by either a bare infinitive ("help reduce") or "in + gerund" ("help in reducing") — both are grammatically acceptable ways to express assistance.

• Always check for parallel structure when two verbs are joined by "and" under a shared modal or auxiliary verb.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
I like played cricket after school.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. playing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "like", when used to express a general habitual preference or enjoyment of an activity, is correctly followed by a gerund (V-ing form).

• Rule: "like" + gerund (V-ing) is used to express enjoyment of or preference for an activity in general, e.g., "I like swimming," "I like reading."

• Applying the rule: "played" (past tense) is grammatically incorrect after "like"; it must be replaced with the gerund "playing".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "play" is incorrect because the bare infinitive form does not correctly follow "like" in this construction expressing general preference.

• Option 3: "played" is incorrect because this is the original erroneous past-tense form, which is grammatically unsound after "like."

• Option 4: "having to play" is incorrect because "having to play" means "being obliged to play," which changes the meaning to obligation rather than enjoyment/preference, and does not fit the intended sense of the sentence.

NOTE

• "Like/love/enjoy/prefer" are commonly followed by a gerund (V-ing) to express general preference — e.g., "I enjoy dancing," "She loves singing."

• Note the distinction: "I like to play cricket" (infinitive, specific occasion/choice) and "I like playing cricket" (gerund, general preference) are both grammatically valid, but not the erroneous past tense "played."

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Bells and whistles
option_1: To take on a difficult task
option_4: Attractive but unnecessary features added to products
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Attractive but unnecessary features added to products.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Bells and whistles" means additional attractive features that are not essential but make something more appealing. (आकर्षक परंतु अनावश्यक विशेषताएँ)
◦ Example: The new smartphone has all the bells and whistles, but I just need one that makes calls reliably.

• The phrase originates from the extra decorative sounds (bells and whistles) added to fairground organs and machines to attract attention, beyond their basic function.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "To take on a difficult task" (मुश्किल काम अपनाना): This is the meaning of a different idiom, such as "to bite the bullet," not "bells and whistles."

• Option 2: "An innovative development" (नवाचार): This is close but incorrect — "bells and whistles" specifically refers to non-essential decorative add-ons, not to genuine innovation.

• Option 3: "At a serious disadvantage" (गंभीर नुकसान की स्थिति में): This meaning corresponds to a different idiom, such as "on the back foot," not "bells and whistles."

NOTE

• Other idioms related to features/appearances often tested in SSC: "Window dressing" (making something appear better than it is), "All that glitters is not gold" (appearances can be deceptive), "Icing on the cake" (an additional good feature on top of something already good).

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement'.
Since my friend was not feeling well, she asked me to come over and take care of her.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. No improvement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "come over" means to visit someone at their home, which fits perfectly with the context of the sentence — the friend wants the speaker to visit and take care of her.

• Since the underlined phrase is already correctly used and conveys the intended meaning, no improvement is required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "come across" is incorrect because this phrasal verb means "to find or encounter something by chance," which does not fit the context of visiting someone.

• Option 3: "come into" is incorrect because this phrasal verb usually means "to inherit" (e.g., "come into money") or "to enter," which does not fit the meaning intended here.

• Option 4: "come through" is incorrect because this phrasal verb means "to survive a difficult situation" or "to be officially received" (e.g., "the results came through"), which does not fit the context of visiting a friend.

NOTE

• Common phrasal verbs with "come" tested in SSC exams: "come over" (visit), "come across" (find by chance), "come up with" (produce an idea), "come down with" (fall ill), "come along" (make progress/accompany).

• Always match the phrasal verb's specific idiomatic meaning to the context of the sentence rather than relying on the base verb's meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Injustice
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Discrimination.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Injustice" means unfair treatment; a violation of someone's rights. (अन्याय)
◦ Example: The workers protested against the injustice of unequal pay for equal work.

• Its closest synonym among the given options is "Discrimination", which means unfair or prejudicial treatment of people, especially based on characteristics like race, age, or gender. (भेदभाव)
◦ Example: The company was sued for gender discrimination in its hiring practices.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Equality" (समानता): This is actually the antonym of "injustice," meaning fair and equal treatment.

• Option 3: "Complacency" (आत्मसंतोष): Means "a feeling of smug self-satisfaction," which is unrelated to the meaning of "injustice."

• Option 4: "Demand" (माँग): Means "an insistent request," which is unrelated to the concept of unfair treatment.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Injustice": unfairness, inequity, prejudice, oppression.

• Antonyms of "Injustice": justice, fairness, equity, impartiality.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Generous
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Mean.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Generous" means willing to give more of something, especially money, than is strictly necessary; kind and unselfish. (उदार)
◦ Example: He is a generous man who donates a large part of his income to charity.

• Its most appropriate antonym among the given options is "Mean", which means unwilling to give or share; stingy; not generous. (कंजूस)
◦ Example: He is too mean to even buy a cup of coffee for his friends.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Needy" (जरूरतमंद): Means "lacking basic necessities of life," which describes a state of poverty, not the opposite of being generous.

• Option 3: "Considerate" (विचारशील): Means "careful not to cause inconvenience to others; thoughtful," which is actually close in spirit to "generous," not its opposite.

• Option 4: "Clever" (चतुर): Means "quick to understand and learn," which is unrelated in meaning to "generous."

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Generous": charitable, liberal, magnanimous, benevolent.

• Other antonyms of "Generous": stingy, miserly, selfish, tight-fisted.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
After finishing all my pending assignments, I plan to ________ in Goa.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. take a holiday.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence states that after finishing all pending assignments, the speaker plans to do something "in Goa," a well-known holiday/tourist destination in India.

• The collocation "take a holiday" means to go on a vacation/break from work, which logically and contextually fits the idea of relaxing in Goa after completing assignments.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "land a meal" is incorrect because this is not a standard English collocation; "land" collocates with things like "land a job" or "land a deal," not "a meal."

• Option 2: "forgive a debt" is incorrect because while grammatically valid as a phrase, it makes no logical sense in the context of finishing assignments and going to Goa.

• Option 4: "go bankrupt" is incorrect because "going bankrupt" means "losing all one's money," which does not logically follow from finishing assignments and going to a holiday destination.

NOTE

• "Take a holiday/vacation," "take a break," and "take time off" are common collocations related to rest and leisure frequently tested in SSC exams.

• Always look for the option that makes the most logical and idiomatic sense within the full context of the sentence, not just grammatical correctness.
